SMTO-UI-0011 — SMTO couldn't copy this text

GUID: e73ff0f0-d83b-4176-a561-1b2854fe9e94
Slug: ui-clipboard-unavailable
Domain: UI · Subsystem: ui

What happened

  • Your browser didn't let SMTO put this text on your clipboard. Nothing else was changed; you can still copy the text yourself.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Highlight the text you want with your mouse, then press Ctrl+C (Windows or Linux) or Command+C (Mac). Copying by hand uses your browser's own Copy command, which works even when SMTO's copy button is blocked.
  2. Click once inside the SMTO page so it's the active window, then try the copy button again. Browsers often refuse to copy for a page that isn't the window you're currently using.
  3. If copy buttons never work, open SMTO through a secure https address or on the same computer, or allow clipboard access for this site in your browser's site settings. Browsers block copy buttons on plain http addresses from another computer and on sites without clipboard permission.

What success looks like

  • When you paste somewhere else, the text you copied appears.

If it still fails

  • Copy the text by hand for now. Ask the person who manages SMTO whether it can be reached over a secure https address.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Copying failed because navigator.clipboard.writeText is unavailable or rejected and the document.execCommand('copy') fallback also failed.

What this means

  • Browser clipboard APIs or the fallback copy command fail to copy the requested text. This presentation or validation result does not establish an external task outcome. Use the saved run, resource revision and receipts when deciding whether an action can safely be repeated.

Why this can happen

  • Browser clipboard APIs or the fallback copy command fail to copy the requested text.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect copy support or permission without assuming the displayed source text is unavailable.

How to fix it

  • The async Clipboard API requires a secure context (HTTPS or localhost) and page focus, and may be blocked by browser permissions or policy; the execCommand fallback can also be disabled. Serve SMTO over HTTPS or localhost, or copy the visible text manually; do not treat a failed copy as success.
  • Select the visible content and copy it with the browser’s supported Copy command.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • A supported manual Copy action copies the intended visible text.

What not to do

  • Do not bypass the unsupported-feature check or reinterpret an unsupported response as success.

Technical notes

  • This presentation or validation result does not establish an external task outcome. Use the saved run, resource revision and receipts when deciding whether an action can safely be repeated.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
